Rashi on Shabbat 45a:1:1.english: One may place a lamp - While it is still day.

Rashi on Shabbat 45a:1:2.hebrew: ע"ג דקל - וידלק שם בשבת, דליכא למיחש לכשיכבה לישקליה מיניה ונמצא משתמש במחובר, דכיון דאקצייה לדבר האסור בין השמשות, איתקצי לכולי יומא:
Rashi on Shabbat 45a:1:2.english: Atop a palm tree - And it may burn there on Shabbat, for there is no concern that when it goes out he will take it from it and thereby be using [something] attached [to the ground]; for since he set it aside for a forbidden purpose at twilight, it is set aside for the entire day.

Rashi on Shabbat 45a:1:3.hebrew: ואין מניחין כו' בי"ט - דשקיל ומנח ליה, ומשתמש באילן:
Rashi on Shabbat 45a:1:3.english: And one may not place, etc., on a Festival - For he might take it and set it down, and [thereby] make use of the tree.

Rashi on Shabbat 45a:1:4.english: What [difference] is there to me [between] Shabbat, etc. - On Shabbat too, he will take it once it goes out.

Rashi on Shabbat 45a:2:1.english: A Hanukkah lamp - After it went out:

Rashi on Shabbat 45a:2:2.hebrew: מקמי חברי - שלא יראוהו בחצר, כדאמרינן בפרקין דלעיל (שבת דף כב:) דנותנו בטפח הסמוך לרשות הרבים, וידעו שהדליקו בו נר, והם גזרו שלא להדליק. אי נמי, ביום חגם אין מניחין לדלוק אור אלא בבית ע"ז:
Rashi on Shabbat 45a:2:2.english: From before the ḥabarei - So that they should not see it in the courtyard, as we say in our chapter above (Shabbat 22b) that one places it within the handbreadth adjacent to the public domain, and they would know that they lit a lamp in it, and they had decreed not to kindle [fires]. Alternatively, on their festival day they do not permit a light to burn except in a house of idol worship.

Rashi on Shabbat 45a:2:3.english: Ḥabarei - The name of a nation that was with the Persians.

Rashi on Shabbat 45a:2:4.english: Is that the halakha - [This was asked] in astonishment.

Rashi on Shabbat 45a:2:5.hebrew: בשעת הדחק - סכנה. אלמא, שלא בשעת הדחק אסור:
Rashi on Shabbat 45a:2:5.english: In exigent circumstances - [Due to] danger. Consequently, when not in exigent circumstances, it is prohibited.

Rashi on Shabbat 45a:3:1.hebrew: שזרען בקרקע - ועדיין לא השרישו, מהו ללקוט ולאכול:
Rashi on Shabbat 45a:3:1.english: That he sowed in the ground - And they have not yet taken root; what is [the ruling regarding whether one may] gather [them] and eat [them]?

Rashi on Shabbat 45a:3:2.hebrew: אין מוקצה לר' שמעון בדבר הראוי - אלא בשמן שבנר בשעה שהוא דולק, כדתניא לעיל:
Rashi on Shabbat 45a:3:2.english: There is no [prohibition of] muktzeh according to Rabbi Shimon regarding an item that is fit [for use] - Except for the oil in a lamp while it is burning, as was taught above.

Rashi on Shabbat 45a:3:3.english: Since it was set aside for its mitzvah - For Shabbat.

Rashi on Shabbat 45a:3:4.english: It was set aside for its prohibition - The prohibition of extinguishing [the flame].

Rashi on Shabbat 45a:4:1.hebrew: והוקצה למצותו לית ליה - בתמיה: דקס"ד שמן שבנר דוקא קאמר, דאיכא תרתי: מוקצה למצוה, ומוקצה של שעת דליקתו משום איסור כיבוי; אבל מוקצה למצוה גרידא לא אסר, ואפילו בשעת המצוה:
Rashi on Shabbat 45a:4:1.english: And does he not hold [of an item] set aside for its mitzva? - [This is asked] in astonishment, for it might enter your mind that he said specifically the oil in the lamp, where there are two [factors]: set-aside for a mitzva, and set-aside at the time of its burning because of the prohibition of extinguishing; but [an object] set aside merely for a mitzva, he did not prohibit, even during the time of the mitzva.

Rashi on Shabbat 45a:4:2.english: Wasn’t it taught: One roofed it - [Referring] to the sukkah, etc.

Rashi on Shabbat 45a:4:3.english: Hangings - Colorful cloths that they call ouvraine [embroidered work].

Rashi on Shabbat 45a:4:6.hebrew: עד מוצאי יו"ט האחרון - והכא מוקצה למצוה איכא, מוקצה דאיסור ליכא. דאי משום סתירת אהל — כי מטא חולו של מועד לשתרי, דומיא דנר שכבה:
Rashi on Shabbat 45a:4:6.english: Until the conclusion of the last Festival day - And here, [the status of] set-aside for a mitzvah is present, [while] set-aside due to a prohibition is not present. For if [it were forbidden] because of dismantling a tent — when the intermediate days of the Festival arrive, it should be permitted, similar to a lamp that went out.

Rashi on Shabbat 45a:5:1.hebrew: והא ממאי דר' שמעון היא - דמותיבנא לך מיניה:
Rashi on Shabbat 45a:5:1.english: And from where [is it known] that it is [according to] Rabbi Shimon - [The baraita] from which I raised an objection to you.

Rashi on Shabbat 45a:5:2.hebrew: דתני ר' חייא כו' אין נוטלין עצים - בפסח ועצרת, מסוכה העשויה לצל, ואפילו נפלו — משום מוקצה, דאיתקצאי מחמת סתירת אהל בי"ט:
Rashi on Shabbat 45a:5:2.english: As Rabbi Ḥiyya taught, etc.: One may not take wood - On Pesach and Atzeret [Shavuot], from a booth constructed for shade; and even if [the pieces of wood] fell [on their own, taking them is forbidden] due to muktzeh, as it was set aside on account of [the prohibition against] dismantling a tent on the Festival.

Rashi on Shabbat 45a:5:3.hebrew: אלא מן הסמוך לה - אם סמך חבילות עצים אצל דופנה, ליכא איסור מוקצה, דדעתיה עילויה מאתמול למישקלינהו למחר, דלא סתר בהו אהלא. ומהך דתני ר' חייא בר יוסף הוי מצי לאותבי ברישא, אלא ניחא ליה לאותבי ממתניתא דר' חייא ור' אושעיא, כדאמרינן בעלמא (חולין דף קמא.): כל מתניתא דלא מיתניא בי ר' חייא כו':
Rashi on Shabbat 45a:5:3.english: Rather, from that which is adjacent to it - If he placed bundles of wood next to its wall, there is no prohibition of set-aside, for his mind was upon them from yesterday to take them tomorrow, since he does not dismantle a tent with them. And from this [baraita] that Rabbi Ḥiyya bar Yosef taught, [the Gemara] could have raised an objection initially; but it preferred to raise an objection from a baraita of Rabbi Ḥiyya and Rabbi Oshaya, as we say elsewhere (Chullin 141a): "Any baraita that was not taught in the academy of Rabbi Ḥiyya, etc."

Rashi on Shabbat 45a:5:4.hebrew: ור' שמעון מתיר - אם נפלה, דלית ליה מוקצה. והכי מוקמינן ליה במסכת ביצה:
Rashi on Shabbat 45a:5:4.english: And Rabbi Shimon permits - [This applies] if it fell, for he does not hold of [the prohibition of] muktzeh; and this is how we establish it in Tractate Beitzah.

Rashi on Shabbat 45a:5:5.hebrew: ושוין בסוכת החג בחג - שהוקצה למצותה, דמצותה כל שבעה. אלמא, כל שעת מצותה נוהג מוקצה שלה, ואע"ג דליכא איסור סתירה:
Rashi on Shabbat 45a:5:5.english: And they agree regarding the sukka of the Festival during the Festival - For it was set aside for its mitzva, as its mitzva [lasts] all seven [days]. Thus, throughout the time of its mitzva its set-aside [status] applies, even though there is no prohibition of dismantling.

Rashi on Shabbat 45a:5:6.hebrew: כעין שמן קאמינא - ולא משום איסור, אלא משום מצוה; דהואיל דהוקצה למצותו דשבת, הוקצה לכל זמן איסור דליקתו, ולא יותר — דאין מצותו אלא בשעת דליקתו, ומשכבה אין בו מצוה. אבל בסוכת החג — מצותה כל שבעה, והקצאתה כל זמן מצותה:
Rashi on Shabbat 45a:5:6.english: I meant [a case] like oil - And [it is] not on account of a prohibition, but rather on account of a mitzvah; for since it was set aside for its Shabbat mitzvah, it was set aside for the entire duration of the prohibition of its burning, and no longer — as its mitzvah is only at the time of its burning, and once it has gone out, there is no mitzvah in it. But regarding the sukkah of the Festival — its mitzvah is all seven [days], and its set-aside status is for the entire duration of its mitzvah.

Rashi on Shabbat 45a:6:1.hebrew: אלא גרוגרות וצמוקין - גרוגרות — תאנים שמעלה לגג ליבשן, ומשנשתהו שם מעט אין ראוים לאכילה עד שיתייבשו; וכן צימוקים דענבים:
Rashi on Shabbat 45a:6:1.english: Except for dried figs and raisins - Dried figs — figs that one brings up to the roof to dry them, and once they have remained there a little [while], they are not fit for eating until they dry; and likewise raisins of grapes.

Rashi on Shabbat 45a:6:2.hebrew: היה אוכל בתאנים - רבותא אשמעי': דהוה אכיל ואזיל — מכיון דאסקינהו, אסח דעתיה ואקצן:
Rashi on Shabbat 45a:6:2.english: [One who] was eating figs - It teaches us a novelty: that [even though] he had been continuously eating [them], once he brought them up [to the roof], he diverted his mind [from them] and set them aside.

Rashi on Shabbat 45a:6:4.hebrew: וכן אתה אומר כו' - ואע"ג דהני חזי כל שעתא, ואפי' נשתהו לא נתקלקלו, מיהו הואיל ואקצינהו — אסירי:
Rashi on Shabbat 45a:6:4.english: And you say the same, etc. - And even though these are fit [for consumption] at all times, and even if they lingered they did not spoil, nevertheless, since he set them aside, they are forbidden.

Rashi on Shabbat 45a:7:1.hebrew: אי נימא ר"י - למה לי הנך דנקט דדחינהו בידים? אפי' הכניסן נמי לאוצר בעו הזמנה:
Rashi on Shabbat 45a:7:1.english: If we say [it is] Rabbi Yehuda - Why do I need these [cases] that it cited, where he rejected them with [his own] hands? Even if he [merely] brought them into a storehouse, they also require designation.

Tosafot on Shabbat 45a:1:1.hebrew: הכי נמי מסתברא דרב כר' יהודה ס"ל - בכמה מקומות אשכחן דרב סבר כר' יהודה: דאסר מטה שייחדה למעות והניח עליה מעות — ואילו לר' שמעון שרי, דהא שרי חצוצרות אפי' תקע בה כמה זימני — ודכרכי דזוזי (לעיל שבת דף יט:); אלא דבעי לאוכוחי דסבר כר' יהודה במיגו דאיתקצאי בין השמשות כו':
Tosafot on Shabbat 45a:1:1.english: "So too, it is reasonable that Rav holds in accordance with Rabbi Yehuda" - In several places we find that Rav holds in accordance with Rabbi Yehuda: as [Rav] prohibited a bed that one designated for money and placed money upon it — whereas according to Rabbi Shimon [it is] permitted, for he permits trumpets even if one blew them several times — and [in the case of] karkhei dizuzei [ship mats] (above, Shabbat 19b); rather, [the Gemara] needed to prove that he holds in accordance with Rabbi Yehuda regarding [the principle of] migo de'itkatzai bein hashemashot [since it was set aside at twilight, it remains set aside for the entire day], etc.

Tosafot on Shabbat 45a:2:1.hebrew: מקמי חברי בשבתא - שביום חג שלהם לא היו מניחין נר אלא בבית ע"ז. ומאי דקמבעיא ליה בנר חנוכה טפי מבנר שבת — משום דלצורך אכילה היו מניחים להם. ואע"ג דבשעת הסכנה אמרינן בבמה מדליקין (לעיל שבת דף כא:) דמניחה על שולחנו ודיו, הכא מיירי אם יארע שלא הניחה על שולחנו. א"נ, אומר ר"י דשעת הסכנה דלעיל לאו סכנת חברים קאמר, אלא סכנת גזירה שגזרו שלא להדליק נר חנוכה:
Tosafot on Shabbat 45a:2:1.english: From before the ḥabarei on Shabbat - For on their festival day, they would not allow a lamp [to remain lit] except in a house of idol worship. And as for why they raised the dilemma concerning a Hanukkah lamp rather than a Shabbat lamp — [this was] because for the need of eating, they would allow them [to keep a light]. And even though during a time of danger we say in [the chapter] Bameh Madlikin (above, Shabbat 21b) that "he places it on his table and that is sufficient for him" [which appears like a light for eating], here it is dealing with [a case where] it happened that he did not place it on his table. Alternatively, the Ri says that "a time of danger" mentioned above did not refer to the danger of the ḥabarei; rather, [it referred to] the danger of a decree, where they decreed not to light Hanukkah candles.

Tosafot on Shabbat 45a:3:1.hebrew: היכא דדחייה בידים אית ליה - ואף על גב דנר שכבה שרי ר' שמעון, אף על גב דדחייה בידים — דהתם שאני, כיון שכבר פסק דיחוי שלה; אבל הכא, לעולם הן דחויין כל זמן שמונחין שם:
Tosafot on Shabbat 45a:3:1.english: "Where he rejected it with his hands, he holds [there is set-aside]" - And even though Rabbi Shimon permits [moving] a lamp that went out, despite the fact that he rejected it with his hands — there it is different, since its rejection has already ceased; but here, they are continuously rejected as long as they remain placed there.

Tosafot on Shabbat 45a:3:2.hebrew: אלא שמן שבנר - לאו דווקא שבנר, דההוא אסור משום מכבה, כדאמר בפ"ב דביצה (דף כב.): "המסתפק ממנו חייב משום מכבה"; אלא המטפטף מנר. ומשום דמוקצה למצותו לא אסור נר הדולק לטלטל, כדפרישית לעיל, אלא כדאמר בסוף פירקין: משום דהוי בסיס לדבר האסור. תימה לר"י: דאמאי נקט "שמן שבנר"? טפי ה"ל למינקט: "אין מוקצה לר' שמעון אלא גרוגרות וצימוקין", דדמו טפי לחיטין שזרען — דלא איתקצאי לא מחמת מצוה ולא מחמת איסור! וליכא למימר דסבר ר' יוחנן דלר' שמעון אין מוקצה בגרוגרות וצימוקין — דהא רבי קאמר בסמוך דאית ליה לרבי שמעון מוקצה בגרוגרות וצימוקין, ומסתמא לא פליג:
Tosafot on Shabbat 45a:3:2.english: Only oil that is in the lamp - [This is] not specifically [referring to oil] that is in the lamp, for that [oil] is forbidden on account of extinguishing, as [the Gemara] says in the second chapter of Beitzah (22a): "One who takes [oil] from it is liable on account of extinguishing"; rather, [it means oil] dripping from the lamp. And [nor can one say that this was stated to explain why the lamp itself is forbidden to be moved, for] on account of [the oil] being set aside for its mitzvah, a burning lamp is not forbidden to be moved, as I explained earlier; rather, as [the Gemara] says at the end of our chapter, [it is forbidden] because it is a base for a forbidden object. The Ri finds it astonishing: Why did [Rabbi Yoḥanan] cite "oil that is in the lamp"? It would have been more appropriate for him to cite: "There is no set-aside according to Rabbi Shimon except for dried figs and raisins," which are more similar to wheat that one sowed, since they were set aside neither on account of a mitzvah nor on account of a prohibition! And it cannot be said that Rabbi Yoḥanan maintains that according to Rabbi Shimon there is no set-aside in [the case of] dried figs and raisins, for Rabbi [Yehuda HaNasi] says nearby that Rabbi Shimon accepts set-aside in the case of dried figs and raisins, and presumably [Rabbi Yoḥanan] does not dispute [him].

Tosafot on Shabbat 45a:4:1.hebrew: עד מוצאי י"ט האחרון של חג - הקשה ר"ת: ביום טוב האחרון, דלא אסר אלא מטעם מיגו דאיתקצאי בין השמשות מחמת יום שעבר — והא רבי שמעון שרי מותר השמן שבנר, אף על גב דהוקצה בין השמשות למצותו משום יום הבא? ונראה לר"י, דבמה שאוסרת הברייתא יום טוב האחרון — לא אתיא כר' שמעון:
Tosafot on Shabbat 45a:4:1.english: "Until the conclusion of the last Festival day of the Festival" - Rabbeinu Tam raised a difficulty: With regard to the last Festival day, where it is forbidden only by reason of "since it was set aside at twilight on account of the day that passed [it is set aside for the entire day]" — but doesn't Rabbi Shimon permit the leftover oil in the lamp, even though it was set aside at twilight for its mitzvah on account of the coming day? And it appears to the Ri that in that which the baraita forbids [them on] the last Festival day, it does not follow Rabbi Shimon.

Tosafot on Shabbat 45a:5:1.hebrew: ולא מן הסמוך לה - בפרק המביא כדי יין (ב. צה ל: ושם) גרס במשנה: "אלא מן הסמוך לה", ופריך בגמ': "והא קסתר אוהלא?", ומשני: "מאי מן הסמוך לה? סמוך לדפנות". והשתא, אי גרס בברייתא דהכא "אלא מן הסמוך לה" — הוי בסמוך לדפנות; ואי גרס "ולא מן הסמוך לה" — מיירי במה שעל הסכך, וטעמא משום דסתר אוהלא, כדאמר התם:
Tosafot on Shabbat 45a:5:1.english: "Nor from that which is adjacent to it" - In the chapter [entitled] HaMevi Kadei Yayin (Beitzah 30b, and there), the version in the Mishnah reads: "Rather, from that which is adjacent to it." And [the Gemara] objects in the Gemara: "But isn't he dismantling a tent?" And it answers: "What is [meant by] 'from that which is adjacent to it'? Adjacent to the walls." And now, if the version in the baraita here reads "Rather, from that which is adjacent to it," it refers to [wood] adjacent to the walls; and if the version reads "Nor from that which is adjacent to it," it deals with that which is upon the roofing [sekhakh], and the reason is because he dismantles a tent, as it says there.

Tosafot on Shabbat 45a:5:2.hebrew: ואם התנה הכל לפי תנאו - בריש המביא (ג"ז שם) פריך עלה: "והא קא סתר אוהלא?" ומוקי לה בסוכה נפולה, וברעועה — דמאתמול דעתיה עלה:
Tosafot on Shabbat 45a:5:2.english: "And if he stipulated, everything is according to his stipulation" - At the beginning of [the chapter entitled] HaMevi ([this too is discussed] there), [the Gemara] raises an objection against it: "But isn't he demolishing a tent?" And [the Gemara] establishes it in [the case of] a fallen sukkah, and [one that was] precarious, for from yesterday his mind was on it.

Tosafot on Shabbat 45a:6:1.hebrew: אלא בגרוגרות וצימוקין - בירושלמי פ' שמסריחין בינתיים. כיון שמתקלקלין כל כך, אין דעתו לקחתם עד שיתקנו היטב:
Tosafot on Shabbat 45a:6:1.english: "Only in [the case of] dried figs and raisins" - In the Yerushalmi it is explained that they emit a foul odor in the interim. Since they spoil so much, one has no intention of taking them until they are thoroughly cured.

Tosafot on Shabbat 45a:6:2.hebrew: וכן אתה אומר באפרסקין - אף על פי שאין מתקלקלין כל כך, מקצה אותם מדעתו:
Tosafot on Shabbat 45a:6:2.english: "And you would say the same with regard to peaches" - Even though they do not spoil so much, [one] sets them aside from his mind.

Tosafot on Shabbat 45a:7:1.hebrew: היכא דלא דחייה בידים אית ליה מוקצה - כגון הא דתנן בפרק מפנין (לקמן שבת קכו:): "ולא את האוצר"; ותנן נמי בפרק בתרא (דף קנו:): "רבי יהודה אומר: אם לא היתה נבלה מע"ש אסורה", כו':
Tosafot on Shabbat 45a:7:1.english: "Where one did not reject it with his hands, he holds [there is] set-aside" - Such as that which we learned in the chapter [entitled] Mefanin (below, Shabbat 126b): "And not the storehouse"; and we also learned in the final chapter (156b): "Rabbi Yehuda says: If it was not a carcass from the eve of Shabbat, it is forbidden," etc.

Tosafot on Shabbat 45a:8:1.hebrew: ואוכל איצטריכא ליה - מדנקט אוכל במוקצה דדחייה בידים, נראה דאזיל ואכיל שרי ליה לר"י במוקצה דלא דחייה בידים, כגון גבי אוצר:
Tosafot on Shabbat 45a:8:1.english: "And [the case of one who was] eating is necessary for it" - From [the fact] that it specified [the case of one who was] eating regarding muktzeh where he rejected it with [his own] hands, it appears that [where] he was in the course of eating, it is permitted according to Rabbi Yehuda in [a case of] muktzeh where he did not reject it with [his own] hands, such as regarding a storehouse.
